executionHistory.summary: Security round over the surface the five bug packets changed, derived from each packet's own commits rather than inherited; for this packet it is rltaxworkspace.js, lifetime-tax-strategy.config.json and lifetime-tax-strategy-lab.html. ONE FINDING IS RECORDED AGAINST THIS PACKET, F-SEC-01, severity medium, not fixed here by design. The bound this packet shipped covers the RESPONSE-HEADER phase only, not the body: loadJson at lifetime-tax-strategy-lab.html:5729-5752 calls window.clearTimeout(timer) in the fulfilment handler, which runs as soon as headers arrive, and only THEN calls response.json(), so the body is streamed with no bound at all. Executed proof, replicating that function's shape byte-for-byte against a local http server with a 1000ms bound: an origin that never sends headers is rejected with AbortError after 1005ms, which is this packet's fix working; an origin that sends 200 headers and then stalls the body mid-JSON was STILL PENDING after 6001ms, six times the bound, with no rejection; a well-behaved origin resolved in 2ms. That reproduces this packet's own stated symptom, a pack origin that accepts the request and never answers suspending the boot chain, on the body rather than on the headers. A second observation on the same field: rltaxworkspace.js:291 admits any finite packReadBoundMs above zero with no ceiling, so 2147483647 was admitted, which is about 24.8 days and is effectively no bound, and 2147483648 was also admitted although it exceeds a 32-bit signed timer; measured in this Node, a 2147483648ms timer fired after 1ms with a TimeoutOverflowWarning, so just past 2^31-1 the bound inverts from unbounded to instant-abort. One simplification was identified in this packet's surface and DECLINED, with the reason recorded rather than the edit made. After the F-SEC-01 restructure, loadJson carries two window.clearTimeout(timer) sites, one in the fulfilment handler of the second .then and one in its rejection handler, which invites collapsing them into a single .finally. It was declined on two independent grounds, either of which is sufficient. First, the two-argument .then(onFulfilled, onRejected) form is SEMANTICALLY different from .finally followed by a rejection handler: in the shipped form the rejection handler cannot see an error thrown by the fulfilment handler beside it, whereas a .finally chain would route such an error into the rejection path and re-label a JSON parse failure as a read failure, which is the boundExceeded-false contract this packet pinned. Second, the two-site shape is pinned from both sides: TB-021-04 asserts the count is exactly 2 and TB-SEC-01-01 additionally asserts that the response-head handler does NOT disarm and that the disarm sits past the parsed body, and TB-SEC-01-01 exists precisely because asserting the count alone would have passed on the original defect, which also had two sites. A refactor that keeps the count while moving the semantics is the failure mode those two assertions were written against. The F-SEC-01 ceiling on rules.packReadBoundMs was audited separately and needs nothing: TIMER_DELAY_CEILING_MS is a single named constant used in the comparison and quoted in the refusal message, the validator is one if / else-if with no overlapping arm, and the constant is consumed by name in scripts/selftest.mjs rather than duplicated as a literal.
